predecessors.name: Starčevo–Körös–Criș culture
predecessors.text: "corresponding mainly to modern-day Serbia and Kosovo, but also parts of Southernmost Hungary, Western-Central Romania", with Bulgaria, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Montenegro also listed; Vinča-Belo…

ledger.x: 5400 BCE: the Vinča culture, with its tells, copper mines and signs, succeeds the Starcevo on the Danube and Morava.
4850 BCE: the Late Vinča period (Vinča D, "4850/4800-4600/4500 BC") begins.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture drawn by modern units and radii, never a frontier.
